result.title: ZOIF: Zeroth-Order Influence Function Estimation for LLM Data Selection Using Only Forward Passes
result.summary: Influence functions enable principled data selection for large language models (e.g., identifying influential training samples for model editing, debugging, or efficient fine-tuning). However, scaling IFs to LLMs is hindered by the intractability of billion-scale Hessian matrices and the prohibitive memory overhead of backpropagation (BP). While many classical IF approximations reduce Hessian complexity, they still rely on BP for gradient computation, requiring massive storage for intermediate activations that impedes practical data selection at scale. To address this, we propose ZOIF, a zeroth-order framework for influence estimation that operates entirely via forward passes, enabling memory-efficient data selection under resource constraints. ZOIF decomposes influence estimation into three BP-free stages: (1) approximating the average proxy gradient via zeroth-order estimation; (2) reformulating and solving the inverse Hessian-vector product as an auxiliary zeroth-order optimization to bypass explicit inversion; and (3) deriving per-sample influence scores via a forward finite difference along the previously computed parameter update direction. Experiments show that ZOIF selects data subsets with downstream utility competitive with, and in some cases exceeding, the evaluated baselines, yet at substantially lower peak memory cost and with comparable overall computation time.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ZOIF，一种只用前向传播的零阶影响函数估计框架：先用零阶估计近似平均代理梯度，再把逆 Hessian 向量积改写为辅助零阶优化，最后沿参数更新方向做前向有限差分得到逐样本影响分数，用于 LLM 数据选择并显著降低峰值显存。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文本身不涉及多模态或 latent 推理，但其无反向传播、低显存的影响估计思路，可能与 LVR 关心的「轨迹训练、贡献分配与监督」问题相关，可供核查其能否迁移到推理轨迹或视觉证据样本的贡献评估。
